proposal:
STATUS. Nothing was executed; every statement is a hand derivation from the supplied code. No polynomial-SAT claim. The invariant is ordered formula caching (Beame, Impagliazzo, Pitassi, Segerlind; cited from memory), not new mathematics.

1. AUDIT.
(a) Soundness. _verify_certificate builds blocks from every original clause. probe gates on set containment and refutes only through an UNSAT 2-SAT quotient. Quotient-stage UNSAT lifts through F(x)=Q(Px) with PL=I. I found no soundness defect in the supplied text.
(b) Work defect, exact cause. step() is memoised on tuple(restrict(state,v,b)), the pre-canonical tuple, while refute and elim_plus depend only on reduced. A state that lacks the branch variable is resubmitted under a new key. Equal canonical formulas reached from different parents hit the cache only when clause order happens to coincide. Assuming the instrumented run used the twin-adjacent order, a hand count with this model reproduces the trusted '4 of 12 repeats' on the Neon58 quotient (8 distinct inputs). Repair: memoise refute and elim_plus on reduced. This is sound because both are deterministic functions of reduced.
(c) windows() truncates after sorting by (size, lexicographic). Standard PHP(6 into 5) has 75 size-2, 100 size-3, 2325 size-4 and 6 size-5 windows (hand count). The cap keeps 75+100+81, so no pigeon clause is tabulated at the root. Independently, at-most-one tables {00,01,10} have full integer hull, so IALH gets no rows there. Its PHP cost is overhead until residuals are tiny.

2. MECHANISM: ORDER IS THE FACTORING. Every full order is sound in run_counting_core, so reordering needs no certificate, checker or Lean obligation. For PT this replaces the contraction rules of the previous two rounds.
Invariant. R_t(F,pi) is the set of non-false canon(F|tau) over assignments tau to the first t variables. ORW(F,pi) = max_t |R_t|.
Lemma A (hand proof). canon(restrict(canon(G),v,b)) = canon(restrict(G,v,b)). Unit closure is confluent, C subset of D survives restriction, and deleting a subsumed clause loses no unit or conflict.
Consequence (canon-only cached search, mra with dispatch). S_t is a subset of R_t. There are at most 2n*ORW canon calls and O(n*ORW^2*(m^2+nm)*w*log n) bit operations including prune.
Lemma B (hand proof, canon-only). PT(k) with twins adjacent has R_t inside {C_s, M_s, Z}: s pairs covered, half-pair zero, some pair zero. So ORW <= 3 for every k. First-members-first gives |R_t| = 2^t up to t=k, and up to t=2k when sides interleave as in Neon58 numbering. That is 4^k, about N^2 for encoded size N. The family separates polynomial degrees only.
Twins merge because every clause containing x contains x', and link(not x) = link(not x'). Then F|x=1 equals F|x=0,x'=1 after subsumption.

3. REPAIR (not implemented): GM-ORDER. At each layer, score each unused variable by the number of distinct non-false canon-only children of the current states. Take the minimum, ties to the smallest ID, then run the pinned step on that variable. One variable per layer keeps the search exact. Scoring costs at most 2n^2*peak canon calls and no IALH. Independent-test prediction: on the 16-variable Neon58 quotient every variable is immediately followed by its twin (the order starts 1, 9) and the peak is 2.

4. FIXTURE (pinned v5). PT(5) with pairs (1,2)...(9,10) and (11,12)...(19,20), ascending order. Hand trace: compression skipped with all_variables_in_odd_blocks; core returns no_clauses_removed; root IALH has no rows; layers [2,1,2,1,2,1,0]; peak 2. Z dies by an empty table on a width-5 negative support, and so does C_4. M_4 dies in elim (DP on 9, 10, 8, then side B). Secondary and fragile: 16 IALH calls, 4 refutations, 10 distinct canonical inputs. Repair 1(b) should give 10 calls.

5. TOTAL WORK. With 1(b), calls <= 2n times the number of distinct canonical states. Each call costs at most 8192 tuples times n UP passes times L literal visits, plus HNF on at most 128 rows (SymPy bit cost uncertified). For PT(k) that is O(k) calls of about N^2 each from quadratic subsumption and DP attempts, so roughly N^2 log N. This is a hand estimate, unverified.

6. NOT HANDLED. Formulas where every order has large ORW and IALH and DP give nothing: PHP needs inequalities, not affine lattices, and random 3-CNF has no merges. Extras that separate twins leave the order sound but useless. Modules whose cofactors merge only after their last variable defeat one-step scoring.
missing_theorem:
MT-A (restricted; elementary; Lean-checkable). Lemma A and the canon-only bound S_t subset of R_t.

MT-B (restricted). Lemma B for PT(k), plus the 2^t count for split twins.

MT-C (the gap for the pinned pipeline; unproved). step is not restriction-commuting. When elim accepts DP steps and still returns STUCK, the stored state is not a canon residue, so equal residues need not give equal states and |S_t| <= |R_t| is unproved. Either prove merge-monotonicity for elim_plus (I expect counterexamples), or store the canon residue and use elim only as a decision test; then calls <= 2n*ORW follows from MT-A. Whether that change raises or lowers peaks is unknown.

MT-D (open). A class where GM's one-step scoring is within a polynomial factor of the minimum ORW over orders. Finding the optimal order is presumably NP-hard (conjecture, by analogy with OBDD ordering).

MT-E (boundary; elementary). A run trace is checkable in time polynomial in its length. So 'every UNSAT CNF has an order with a polynomial trace' implies NP=coNP. Any universal bound for this architecture is at least that hard. I do not claim it.
self_attack:
1. ORW is OBDD width for clause residues. The result is a restricted theorem plus an ordering heuristic.
2. PT never separated polynomial from exponential: the bad order costs about N^2 states. The gain is a degree.
3. GM is myopic. A 3-variable multiplexer module has four distinct cofactors after two variables, so its variables tie with unrelated ones and IDs decide. Lookahead of depth d costs n^d.
4. The fixture trace depends on hand analysis of UP tables and DP acceptance. If IALH refutes M_1 or C_1 the peak is 1. If DP accepts a step in M_3 the layers change. Call counts depend on tuple order.
5. The PHP window count assumes the standard encoding and explains at most part of the timeout. SymPy overhead per window may dominate.
6. MT-C may be false, and decide-only elim may lose merges that DP currently creates.
mechanism_signature: Certificate-free ordering: greedy minimum-fanout variable choice scored by canon-only residue merging; ordered residue width ORW as the work invariant; restriction-commutation of canon; canonical-key memoisation of IALH and DP. Exact for PT(k) (ORW <= 3). No bound for general CNF; the universal statement implies NP=coNP.
delta_from_prior: Rounds 104-105 and Fable73 factored modules by contraction with new certificates. This round needs none. (1) Order alone gives ORW <= 3 on PT(k), with a proof sketch. (2) The exact code cause of repeated IALH calls, matching the trusted 4-of-12 count. (3) The commutation lemma that turns residue counts into a call bound, and the precise reason it fails for the pinned elim step. (4) The observation that PT's bad order is only quadratic in encoded size. (5) The PHP window-truncation count. (6) The NP=coNP boundary for any universal ORW claim.
